title: Quantum Soundness of a Total-Degree Line-versus-Point Test
abstract: We prove quantum soundness of the total-degree diagonal line-vs-point test using the individual-degree soundness theorem of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen. A random change of coordinates yields projective polynomial decoders of total degree at most $md$. The uniform-line slice of the test bounds the weight of outcomes of degree greater than $d$, which are removed by a common relabeling. This reduction does not yield a dimension-independent soundness bound: the $\operatorname{poly}(m)$ dependence of the individual-degree theorem persists, as discussed in Section 1.2 of arXiv:2009.12982.
summary: This theoretical paper proves the quantum soundness of a specific quantum test called the total-degree diagonal line-versus-point test. It achieves this by mathematically reducing the complex total-degree test to a known individual-degree soundness theorem. The work is significant for establishing the security and reliability of quantum protocols based on polynomial constraints.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove the quantum soundness of the total-degree diagonal line-versus-point test.
main_result: It establishes the quantum soundness of this test by reducing it to an existing individual-degree soundness theorem, although the resulting bound retains a polynomial dependence on the dimension $m$.
method: The proof employs a random change of coordinates and utilizes a reduction strategy that leverages the individual-degree soundness theorem, combined with bounding techniques for high-degree outcomes.
model_or_system: The analysis is set up in a two-prover quantum test scenario involving measurements on a shared entangled state $|\psiangle$. The test itself is the total-degree diagonal line-vs-point test.

why_interesting: While highly abstract, the techniques used for bounding quantum correlations and establishing soundness in quantum testing protocols are foundational to quantum information theory and cryptography.
